[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Callbacks, Observers, and Lifecycle Hooks in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ruby on Rails provides powerful mechanisms to hook into the lifecycle of Active Record models. These hooks allow you to execute custom logic before or after database operations such as creation, updates, and destruction."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Active Record Lifecycle Hooks"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Active Record objects go through a well-defined lifecycle managed by Rails. As records are created, updated, or destroyed, several events trigger callbacks. You can tie your own methods to these events to handle validation, logging, or associated record maintenance."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Creation Lifecycle: before_validation, after_validation, before_save, around_save, before_create, around_create, after_create, after_save, after_commit / after_rollback."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Update Lifecycle: before_validation, after_validation, before_save, around_save, before_update, around_update, after_update, after_save, after_commit / after_rollback."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Destruction Lifecycle: before_destroy, around_destroy, after_destroy, after_commit / after_rollback."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Callbacks in Models"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To use a callback, declare it as a class method inside your Active Record model. Below is an example demonstrating common callback declarations."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"class Article < ApplicationRecord
  before_validation :normalize_title, on: [:create, :update]
  after_create :send_welcome_notification
  before_destroy :ensure_not_published

  private

  def normalize_title
    self.title = title.strip.capitalize if title.present?
  end

  def send_welcome_notification
    UserMailer.welcome_email(self.user).deliver_later
  end

  def ensure_not_published
    if published?
      errors.add(:base, "Cannot delete a published article")
      throw(:abort)
    end
  end
end"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Halting Execution with throw(:abort)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When using 'before_' callbacks, you can halt the entire operation (such as saving or destroying a record) by throwing the symbol ':abort'. This will cause the save method to return false and trigger a rollback if inside a transaction."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"The Role of Observers"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Historically, Rails used the 'rails-observers' gem to extract business logic out of models and into separate observer classes. While extracted from core Rails, observers are still useful for adhering to the Single Responsibility Principle, separating cross-cutting concerns like emailing or caching from model data integrity."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Callbacks"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep callbacks small and delegate complex business logic to service objects or domain models."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid making external API requests inside critical callbacks unless wrapped in background jobs (like Active Job) to prevent request blocking."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be cautious with conditional callbacks ('if' and 'unless' options) to avoid unexpected state mutations during test suites."}]
